clue.text: What some ancient citizens wore to talk

parts.note: taken as written
gas is informal for idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: A question about what a Roman citizen would put on for making a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the formal garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: One held by the bridge player

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: held by means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone holding cards at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge player' suggests the card game; 'player' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, someone who plays parts on stage.

clue.text: Feel satisfied, say, having dashed all round the world

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so only its sound counts

parts.note: to glow is to feel warm contentment
bally and dashed are both old British euphemisms for bloody

explanation.surface: Someone glows with satisfaction after rushing right round the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' looks like hurrying; it is the mild oath, as in 'a dashed nuisance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Globally means throughout the whole world.

clue.text: He practises pronunciation at first with the injured

definitions.text: He practises pronunciation at first with the injured

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
at first means take only the opening letter of pronunciation

explanation.surface: A clinician works on speaking clearly with patients who have been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges HE PRACTISES, P (the first letter of 'pronunciation') and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech therapist treats speaking problems, often with people recovering from injury.

clue.text: Lover boy's weapon that made one's lip curl

definitions.meaning: the archer god of love carries a bow
the double curve of the upper lip is named after that god's bow

explanation.surface: The god of love's weapon somehow made someone sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper lip's double curve is named after the love god's bow, so the phrase means both the weapon and the lip shape.

clue.text: Jug holds litre, enough for the family

indicators.note: holds means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a can is a container for liquid, like a jug

explanation.surface: A jug containing a litre is enough to serve a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is an extended family group, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Current occasion for lots of give and take?

definitions.text: occasion for lots of give and take?
definitions.meaning: a birthday or Christmas, when presents are exchanged

explanation.definitionFit: Present-day means modern, and humorously a day when presents are given and received.

clue.text: Go at reduced rate to this play?

definitions.text: Go at reduced rate to this play?

parts.words: Go at reduced rate to this play?
parts.note: a road sign telling drivers to slow down for a hazardous bend, which is also the title of a J B Priestley play

explanation.definitionFit: Priestley's 1932 drama has a title that drivers would take as a reason to slow down.

clue.text: Cash machine in bar gives help to one in a mess?

definitions.text: help to one in a mess?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to bar is to ban
ATM is short for automated teller machine, a cash dispenser

explanation.surface: A cashpoint in a pub helps someone in financial trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess here is the officers' dining hall, not a muddle; a batman is an officer's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman is a soldier who acts as an officer's personal servant, an officer being one who eats in the mess.

clue.text: Maybe port's situated round end of old town

indicators.note: situated round means placed around another piece

parts.note: port is an example of wine, and the plural form gives wines

indicators.note: end of means take the last letter of the word old

explanation.surface: A port lies near the far end of an old town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests a harbour; it is the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Widnes is a town in Cheshire, north-west England, on the River Mersey.

clue.text: Without a single amount to be paid, i.e. free of charge

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex dividend
a single thing is one
a rate is a charge or fee to be paid

explanation.surface: A bill explained as costing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free of charge' looks like 'costing nothing', but here it means cleared of an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of a criminal charge or blame.

clue.text: Recorded a short number that's oddly trendy

parts.note: No. is the short form of number

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of the word trendy

explanation.surface: A brief number that charted was oddly fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noted has been written down, that is recorded.

clue.text: After removing head, cook special fish

indicators.note: to cook figures or books is to rearrange them, so these letters are shuffled
removing the head of the word special drops its first letter

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: chop off the head, then cook the special fish of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After removing head' takes S from SPECIAL to leave PECIAL, which 'cook' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a common European flatfish eaten widely in Britain.

clue.text: For instance, a party making comeback can achieve power

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the pieces are read backwards from end to start

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: A political party staging a comeback can win power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a political party, but it is a revel; 'making comeback' turns everything before it, end to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is influence or power used to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Dire photos developed in cleric's office

indicators.note: photos are developed, and here the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bad pictures were processed in a vicar's study.
explanation.definitionFit: The priesthood is the office or position of a priest.

clue.text: A lecturer's first educated class about poetic device?

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the word lecturer

parts.note: the literati are the educated, literary class
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A lecturer's first lesson to an educated class concerns a poetic technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had stray letters S and G; the page prints none.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliteration, repeating opening consonants, is a technique used in poetry.

clue.text: Hurry up with baby carrier for tiny tot

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to run is to hurry
a sling is a fabric carrier for a baby

explanation.surface: A parent rushing along with a baby sling for a toddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursling is an infant still being nursed, a small child.

clue.text: Teacher's favourite learner kept in, having written words wrongly

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a female teacher

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
L is the learner symbol on British L-plates

explanation.surface: The teacher's pet was kept in detention after spelling badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' suggests detention; it puts L inside PET.
explanation.definitionFit: To misspell is to write words with the wrong letters.

clue.text: Champagne's indefinable quality

parts.note: Champagne is a French region, so its phrase for a quality hard to put into words is a French expression meaning I do not know what

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally says I don't know what, and is used for an elusive, hard-to-describe charm.

clue.text: It may be found among herbal samples

definitions.text: It may be found among herbal samples

indicators.note: found among means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark about what might be discovered in plant specimens.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic resin, and also a plant, so it might well be in herbal samples.

clue.text: One might catch the sun a bit

definitions.meaning: a sixpenny bit, an old British coin

explanation.definitionFit: A sunbather tans, and a tanner was slang for the old British sixpence coin.

clue.text: Porter brings in a trolley with various dishes to order

indicators.note: brings in means the other pieces are put inside

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
a cart is a trolley

explanation.surface: A porter wheels a trolley of assorted dishes for diners ordering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a hotel worker; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a la carte means ordering individual dishes from the menu rather than a set meal.

clue.text: Drinker reels, imbibing no end of wine… during these?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside
a drinker who reels spins round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers, gulping wine during the speeches at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reels' turns the drinker round, and the wine trimmed by 'no end of' goes inside; 'these' points back to the scene, the toasts drunk at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: These points back to the whole picture: toasts are the occasions when drinkers raise glasses together.

clue.text: A ranch miles away, at such a distance?

indicators.note: away means taken off, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a ranch is a farm

explanation.surface: A ranch many miles off, so far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means from or at a great distance.

clue.text: Form of religion popular with students, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' body

explanation.surface: A faith that, after some thought, students find appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reads as 'after thought', but it turns both pieces round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunni is the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

clue.text: Unpleasant drive

definitions.meaning: a military push or attack, as in launching a campaign

explanation.definitionFit: Offensive means repugnant, and as a noun an attacking campaign or push.

clue.text: Army routed in struggle to depose English monarch

indicators.note: an army in a struggle is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged
to depose is to remove from power, so a letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A defeated army fights to overthrow an English king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to depose' removes E (English) from ARMYROUTED before 'in struggle' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Tudor, Mary I, was Queen of England from 1553 to 1558.

clue.text: OK to produce script for radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so a word that sounds like another is meant

parts.note: to produce script is to write

explanation.surface: Approval given to write a script for broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Right can be said as an interjection meaning all right or OK.
